markdown: ## Watchlist - **UniCredit:** It has reached broad agreement with Germany on its Commerzbank takeover, according to Reuters sources [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxNbzY3bmFvcDFWWmUtWmRlTkg1OElfODl6Z1BCWG1LQlp3U0xsbXktUlo3SXRKczAxdEI2bGRSTmxLRDUwMXRMZU9LOGJuX0QyTkxLNHVnS254WkF6MVNRNmNsUkxZRXZreWh2d0R5M2JmZk1pUWZHYVg0R1BjUDBXNVlFOXpZRGhtRUxLd1F6UnViV0VQcHBGSWw0VjF4ZUU2dk9zQ3liMzNmY3k0TExRXzlVMA?oc=5). That removes the last big political hurdle, so finalise plans for combined counterparty limits and any account migrations. - **JPMorgan:** The outages that hit several US banks this week were caused by a software bug at JPMorgan Chase [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48778/us-bank-outages-caused-by-software-bug-at-jpmorgan-chase?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). Experts suggest the recent rash of outages may stem from firms rushing to patch issues identified by AI. Confirm that any delayed Carrier payments were caught and reconciled, and test second-bank contingency. - **JPMorgan:** It is offering steep price cuts to revive a stalled $2bn "hung" software debt sale at a double-digit yield [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/16a99ff4-6060-4c81-8c4f-7e43503e4a11?syn-25a6b1a6=1). Bank risk appetite for leveraged tech credit is weak, a sign of tighter credit conditions at the riskier end of the market. - **BNP Paribas:** Its Italian bank, BNL, will cut branches and target wealthier clients [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxNMF96S0Y3NUc2MEZtWnhTdmtkSnVHQkV1dlNoWGVCaUJ0UlNzZU5lcE9wNlhEalBpZnByc195aTdRVUlXcEozTXEzVjB2RlhnSDMxdnIyMmItd2NrMmpULWhlUm9vTXVMbnVIcnM3YmxidGhxTWkzVjV1SDA1d3VpLXZ5QXVTMVlwRTAwT1gtcnBMamRNMS1FME02bW5KN0c0ajdpbndjQTB1MjA0aEhaZHF3Tm43aW8?oc=5). This is a retail-focused move, with no direct impact expected on corporate cash management. ## The brief - **Fed minutes show officials expect more rate hikes and worry about AI's impact on inflation** [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/fed-minutes-october-2026.html). Waller says the Fed may need to "shock people" with a half-point hike [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/federal-reserve-governor-christopher-waller.html). Model a 50bp December move for SOFR-linked debt and intercompany loans. - **Euro-zone inflation has hit 4%, paving the way for more ECB hikes** [The Irish Times](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxNYWYwcndGUmpIcTJCdFU1eVFBbUxQVDhySy1aeTdFbDFmNkhXRXlLRnJ5cThPeldEdHc5U2htdHN1MENDa1BfZkRmWEpvN2traVhSNE0xaHFOUTdaQzU1R1NvSXp4Y0ZDeUluVnAwTmszZXZGZVZkbzBHM0V6Q3lScFIxWEJyVlZvcFVlMEdWNjctRDdodWJSSDl3NWtyUUpyTGhiM0xGX0dwaU43cXc?oc=5). Vujcic says a hike is likely next month and more may follow [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxQRnlHUnBfdlFRc2hJbXowTTlOejg0Z0xSMm1nYlI2RmVDNDhLTVM2eTQxRHlXdTNtRU1YaEhhY3kzckpxd3VFU1R0eDFnZnFlZ1hMTWFDMzBhZHF1N0otNzd1b0tMN0t5R09aX3BrNkVKSE9jdmRubmZjM1JsQi1acVhJOU9uU20zYlJ2R1hVNmZzZGRIR1JNa1ZycGpWT1N3Yy1GU1NOanFjU2xVUGRBMk5hNEo?oc=5). Keep euro surplus cash on short, rolling tenors to capture the increases. - **The ECB will discuss raising banks' reserve requirement next week, according to sources** [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxNNlY3ckxpdlVSS1dCVmhacndwQnBDTFBtRTVhVjJGOEJwdlVkUlVPRjJ5MUZTdE51WDRXNXNjQ25Zd3M4WEd5N2pvdjNxZzIyUU9wLW1uakxQN1E1YWhCX0JtN2dpZk5jUl9RX2s5SnI3RThHbnRXTlBoMnBfdVF4dlVQQW5RTUhwU25vNlFQbVplUWI5SjBRdUt2Y28xc0M1WmZSNmhNUm5qU2Y5a0tJc0lYLTg?oc=5). Higher reserve requirements could tighten euro liquidity and change how much banks pay on corporate deposits, so watch deposit pricing from euro-zone banks. - **Trump, Xi and Putin are expected to hold a rare trilateral meeting today in China** [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/trump-xi-putin-apec-shenzhen-china.html). Any shift on tariffs or sanctions could move CNY, energy and supply-chain costs quickly, so be ready to refresh assumptions. ## Rates & FX - **The dollar is still climbing.** EUR/USD is 1.0968 (-1.43% on the week) and GBP/USD is 1.3168 (-1.04%). Barclays and Deutsche Bank see the AI boom extending dollar strength [Bloomberg](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxPUndMRVIwUkE3WWdNbkdNUHo0VElVU2stU3RUU2tKamVMOVFuNkJfZEQwMWhPQm1jSG5uQ0U1YWhDdDI5UzkwVk9aR2duNGxZcm0yLXNpZ3FTMHVNQl9hcnpwSUlMNkllTkFDaUpLZzRjV1hRUGNJSDhNSFh3VGhoTnZ6WVBrZ1c5NWg1Qk91SVNGQm9sYmwyQ091QWtjWW82Wkw2cXRLakRpWTFuNVA0aQ?oc=5). Consider layering in more cover on European earnings. - **Gold has dropped to a 14-month low as the dollar and yields rise on hawkish Fed rhetoric** [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxQVlk2MG4xbDV2emVoNk9vRVhTcTlRbkZLMDgwMjBMTEdVeXFDV21zX0NVdmF0YzQzRDZ4TkowaDJQQlZlTDBsbm9BWHFXNXpYZzVVejAtTGRZTTFHRjV4dllJV0ZxVzVvbVJCN1lxdk50NXVaNkRxTGJQbDYyZjhNNElTUElOWVU0eW0ySnBRMndSU1ZrTGE4ZlNMdDk0UXVmUjZLSEVfQlc?oc=5). The 10-year Treasury is 5.07% (-3bp) and the 2-year is 4.80%. SOFR is 3.92%. - **Other currencies and rates.** USD/MXN rose 0.61% to 18.576, so the peso weakened on the day. USD/JPY is 159.42, USD/CNY is 6.6672 and EUR/GBP is 0.8329. €STR is 2.441% and SONIA is 3.9833%. - **No high-impact data today.** China's loan prime rates are due at 01:00 Dublin on Friday, forecast unchanged at 3.00% and 3.50%. A surprise cut would signal more support for China's slowing economy. ## Also worth knowing - **The World Bank is working with Citi and Circle to test stablecoins for development payments** [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48780/world-bank-partners-citi-and-circle-to-test-stablecoins-for-development-payments?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). - **Goldman Sachs has led a $280m Series C for European fintech Payhawk, at a $2bn valuation** [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48775/goldman-sachs-leads-280m-series-c-for-payhawk?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). - **UK regulators have told City firms to tighten their cyber defences as AI exposes vulnerabilities** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/7cd81085-95d0-4511-b640-300a2c8791ff?syn-25a6b1a6=1). - **Deutsche Bank's Italian unit hid up to €800m of mortgage lending losses**, according to the FT [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/06be5c7d-b1f2-44e9-9cad-a2dcb5a2f452?syn-25a6b1a6=1). ## Worth thinking about Headroom on the winter grid could change how contractors sell heat pumps [ACHR News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNcEpzVjNJSFl0RlBNOXRRQmpZV3FnNEJ1UW9HUy1hdFFTQU16amFtNTVyVS1Ja1lYRV9KT0ZNYzRGNmZYRDVoMTdHc1pUZGlCS3RDQk1FX2J5Y1RxamhUaWQxX1BPT2R6WF9POHhPYjdIZ3FEdS1TY2UxTnI2MFZfeVRZbGtZNzZVZEUtNUJwaC1QdlJZeldqYTYwM3RoLTVabG16S0hHNjgyQQ?oc=5). Meanwhile, US companies are turning to robots to ease a labour shortage [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/747f5533-1bab-4143-a78b-ed4e2b575340?syn-25a6b1a6=1). For FP&A, both point to demand and cost shifts that could move quickly, so check whether the 2027 plan has enough flexibility in inventory and working capital to respond.
